anomalies.observed: On the CAN differential pairs (the lines running from the isolated CAN transceivers U16/U9 to the M12 CAN connectors J16 'CAN Interface A' and J22 'CAN Interface B') the only passive components shown are the 120R termination resistors R75/R29 behind SW5; no CDSOT23-SM712 (or any other TVS/ESD) diode array is drawn anywhere on the CAN0/CAN1 pair nets across the CAN BUS sheets.
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table states that D9 and D10, CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays, are placed on CAN0_P/N and CAN1_P/N for CAN-bus transient/ESD protection, and that this matches the documented intended part family (twistedfields-notes.txt 'TVS Diodes: SM712-TP or SM712-02HTG').

evidence.quote: D9, D10 — CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N | CAN bus transient/ESD protection | docs/twistedfields-notes.txt lists "TVS Diodes: SM712-TP or SM712-02HTG" as the intended part family for this role; the netlist's CDSOT23-SM712 matches this documented choice.
CAN BUS sheets: transceiver outputs to J16/J22 carry only R75 120R / R29 120R (SW5 termination); no SOT23 TVS array symbol appears on the CAN pair nets.

anomalies.impact: The two external CAN buses lose the specified transient/ESD protection. Normal communication is unaffected, but the CAN transceivers and the long motor-controller cabling are no longer clamped against surges/ESD as intended, so a bus transient can damage the front-end or corrupt frames — a deviation from the documented protection scheme.

parsed.summary: The build matches the spec on every functional block I could verify (16 MHz CAN crystals, MCP2515 + isolated transceivers, SN74LVC1G07 e-stop sinks, LTC4412 + P-MOS ideal diode, ISL54222 muxes, WS2812B string, CM4 pin mapping cross-checked against the Hirose mirror), but the CDSOT23-SM712 TVS arrays the spec places on the CAN differential pairs are absent from the drawing, leaving CAN0/CAN1 without the documented transient/ESD protection.
